statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-55199: a malicious server can make a client spin in a CPU loop by sending SSH_MSG_EXT_INFO with a huge extension count, because the handler in src/packet.c ignored _libssh2_get_string() failures. It is fixed upstream by https://github.com/libssh2/libssh2/commit/17626857d20b3c9a1addfa45979dadcee1cd84a4 (https://github.com/libssh2/libssh2/pull/1864), and Alpine lists it as fixed in 1.11.1-r3 in the secfixes of its libssh2 recipe (https://gitlab.alpinelinux.org/alpine/aports/-/blob/3.23-stable/main/libssh2/APKBUILD). We checked every published libssh2 build for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository, 1.11.1-r1 to 1.11.1-r5, on x86_64 and aarch64, each verified against its index checksum: the shared library /usr/lib/libssh2.so.1.0.1 (libssh2) and the static library /usr/lib/libssh2.a (libssh2-static), with function boundaries taken from the libssh2-dbg debug symbols and from the static library's symbol table. _libssh2_packet_add(), which holds the SSH_MSG_EXT_INFO handler, changes size between 1.11.1-r2 and 1.11.1-r3 on both architectures and is byte-identical in the static library from 1.11.1-r3 to 1.11.1-r5. 1.11.1-r3 is the first fixed build, and every later build carries the fix.

CVE-2026-55199: in libssh2 through 1.11.1, the SSH_MSG_EXT_INFO handler in _libssh2_packet_add() (src/packet.c) ignores the return values of _libssh2_get_string(), so a malicious server can make a client keep looping over a large claimed extension count and spin the CPU before authentication. It is fixed upstream by https://github.com/libssh2/libssh2/commit/17626857d20b3c9a1addfa45979dadcee1cd84a4 (https://github.com/libssh2/libssh2/pull/1864). Two builds of this owner are published in the DHI Alpine 3.24 repository, 1.96.0-r0 and 1.96.1-r0, each as the rust and cargo packages for x86_64 and aarch64; all eight packages were unpacked and every ELF file in them was searched for libssh2 code. In 1.96.0-r0, /usr/bin/cargo has libssh2 compiled in statically through the libssh2-sys 0.3.1 crate, which bundles the libssh2 1.11.1 release (commit a312b43): the program carries the banner SSH-2.0-libssh2_1.11.1_DEV, does not list libssh2.so.1 among its needed libraries, and contains error messages from libssh2's src/packet.c and src/transport.c. The libssh2 source in libssh2-sys 0.3.1 (https://crates.io/crates/libssh2-sys/0.3.1) still discards those return values in the handler, and the program contains the handler's own error message, Invalid extension info received, so 1.96.0-r0 is affected. In 1.96.1-r0, cargo is linked against the system libssh2 instead (it needs libssh2.so.1, supplied by the separate libssh2 package) and contains no copy of libssh2: neither the banner nor any of the src/packet.c messages found in 1.96.0-r0 is present. Alpine made that change in its rust 1.96.1-r0 recipe and lists this CVE as fixed there: https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/commit/0f7dfa74845f47bc7ae7251e07fd7d68716870b8. The rust package of both builds contains no libssh2 code. 1.96.1-r0 is the first build of this owner without the vulnerable code.

CVE-2026-55199: a malicious server can make a client spin in a CPU loop by sending SSH_MSG_EXT_INFO with a huge extension count, because the handler in src/packet.c ignored _libssh2_get_string() failures. It is fixed upstream by https://github.com/libssh2/libssh2/commit/17626857d20b3c9a1addfa45979dadcee1cd84a4 (https://github.com/libssh2/libssh2/pull/1864). Debian fixed it for trixie in 1.11.1-1+deb13u1 (DSA-6365-1, https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-55199). We checked every published libssh2 build for Debian 13 based on 1.11.1-1+deb13u1 or later in the DHI Debian repository, on amd64 and arm64, each verified against its index checksum: the shared library libssh2.so.1.0.1 (libssh2-1t64), the static library libssh2.a (libssh2-1-dev) and the libssh2-1t64-dbgsym debug symbols. Each build's Debian changelog includes the 1.11.1-1+deb13u1 security update entry naming this CVE. _libssh2_packet_add(), which holds the SSH_MSG_EXT_INFO handler, is byte-identical in the static library across all of these builds on each architecture. The range's fixed version is the first DHI build of 1.11.1-1+deb13u1, and every later build carries the fix.
